booklet.title: xmldocs: one XML source, two views
booklet.author: Giovanni Porcari

purpose.p: xmldocs is an experimental Claude Code skill. It starts from the thesis of The Unreasonable Effectiveness of HTML (Thariq Shihipar, Anthropic): for documents an agent writes for people, HTML works better than Markdown.

It tries a middle way. The information stays in typed XML, where it is more structured and easier to search than in Markdown or HTML. The visual enrichment is delegated to XSLT, which generates from each XML an HTML view for people and a compact Markdown view for LLMs, the chat and GitHub.

row.cell: the LLM that writes or edits
Single source. Metadata as attributes, validated by XSD and Schematron.
the LLM that reads; people in the chat or on GitHub
Compact view with all the metadata. The cheapest format to read.
Full reading: facts, rules and decisions set apart visually, diagrams drawn.

list.item: uv, which installs lxml for the script in an isolated environment.
A browser with network access for the Mermaid diagrams of the HTML view, loaded from jsdelivr.

step.title: Understand why the source is XML
step.p: Many sentences of a project document carry metadata: where a fact comes from, how it was verified, whether a decision is open.
In XML the metadata are attributes. In Markdown they become sentences: an LLM has to interpret them and no program can check them.

example.title: The same fact in both formats
example.code: <fact source="kajenn/src/kajenn/server.py:416" method="read" verified="2026-10-10"> The cleanup of <c>request.db</c> runs on the event loop.</fact>
Read in the code on 2026-10-10 (`kajenn/src/kajenn/server.py:416`): the cleanup of `request.db` runs on the event loop.

step.p: Attributes allow three things Markdown does not:

list.item: Validation. The XSD refuses a fact without a source. Schematron refuses a plan phase started while a decision it needs is still open.
Filtered views. The script can show one part only, for example the decisions.
Document types. Each type has required parts: a booklet without steps is invalid.

step.title: Understand why XML is not enough
step.p: XML costs more tokens than Markdown, and people do not read it willingly.
To read, an LLM spends less with the Markdown view than with the XML. The Markdown view keeps every metadata as a short label.
People read the HTML view better: RUN, TEST and READ labels, colours for rule levels and decision states, drawn diagrams.

The price is richness. The HTML of the article is made to measure for each document. The HTML of xmldocs comes from a fixed template per type and is static. For the cases the vocabulary cannot express there is embed.

step.title: Put the files in the right place
step.p: The three files sit in the same folder. Only the XML is edited.
step.code: xmldocs/<type>/<name>.xml source xmldocs/<type>/<name>.md generated xmldocs/<type>/<name>.html generated
step.p: Public types (booklet, proposal) live in xmldocs/ and are committed. Private types (plan, handoff, note) live in temp/xmldocs/, which git ignores.

step.title: Write, validate, generate
step.code: uv run --script skills/xmldocs/scripts/xmldocs.py check xmldocs temp/xmldocs uv run --script skills/xmldocs/scripts/xmldocs.py render xmldocs temp/xmldocs
step.p: check applies the type's XSD, the embed check and the Schematron rules. render writes .md and .html beside every XML.

step.title: Add hand-made SVG or HTML for edge cases
step.p: An embed holds SVG or HTML in CDATA and is inserted as is into the HTML view. It is visual only: the required summary carries the information in text, and the Markdown view shows title and summary.

example.title: An SVG embed
example.code: <embed kind="svg" id="e-threads" title="One connection per thread" summary="Each pool thread has its own connection; the event loop has none."> <![CDATA[ <svg viewBox="0 0 420 130"> … </svg> ]]> </embed>

step.p: Colours come from the page variables (var(--fg), var(--panel), …), so the embed follows light and dark mode.
Script tags, on…= handlers and javascript: URLs are refused unless the embed says scripts="true". With it, check prints a warning and the HTML marks the embed SCRIPT.

step.title: Show a document in the chat
step.code: uv run --script skills/xmldocs/scripts/xmldocs.py show temp/xmldocs/handoff/2026-10-10.xml --part next uv run --script skills/xmldocs/scripts/xmldocs.py show xmldocs/booklet/kajenn-app.xml --diagrams
step.p: show prints the Markdown view and writes no file. In the chat a diagram or an embed becomes one placeholder line, because the chat does not draw Mermaid.
--diagrams prints the Mermaid sources and the embeds. They are shown with an inline HTML widget, starting from references/mermaid-widget.html.
step.diagram: flowchart LR X[name.xml] -->|check| V{XSD + Schematron} V -->|render| H[name.html] V -->|render| M[name.md] V -->|show| C[Markdown in the chat] V -->|show --diagrams| W[widget in the chat]

rules.rule: Edit only the XML, and regenerate .md and .html after every change.

rule.why: A statement not verified against a source is not a fact.

rules.rule: Verify every fact with tools before writing it.
Write code, diagram and embed bodies in CDATA.

rule.why: uv falls back to the enclosing project when the script path does not exist, and creates its uv.lock and .venv.

rules.rule: Run the script with uv run --script and an absolute path.
Name a private document in a public one.

rule.why: They are Mermaid keywords: the diagram is not drawn.

rules.rule: Use loop, alt, opt, par, end or note as participant names in a sequence diagram.

limits.limit: The script does not detect Mermaid syntax errors: Mermaid runs in the browser. A diagram is checked by opening the HTML.
The side panel of the desktop app may show a local HTML file as a static snapshot. Mermaid does not run there and the diagram stays as source.
XSD 1.0 has no assertions. Rules between attributes are in Schematron (schema/rules.sch).
In the chat, links between documents cannot be followed. The Markdown view shows an internal reference as text followed by (→ id).
The fixed labels of the views are in English only. A per-language file that redefines them is planned, not written.
The content of an embed is not validated: broken HTML breaks the page.

facts.fact: Same handoff: hand-written Markdown 1,139 tokens, XML 1,742, HTML 4,070 (1,530 of them CSS), generated Markdown view 1,234. Claude's tokenizer was not available: the ratios are indicative.
The generated Markdown view carries source, method and date of 12 facts; the hand-written handoff carries the source of some and the method of none.
A ```mermaid block in the reply text appears as code. The same source in an inline HTML widget is drawn.
With the base theme in dark mode, participant boxes have unreadable text until actorBkg and actorTextColor are set.
An SVG embed using the page variables is readable in light and dark mode; an HTML embed with scripts="true" runs its script.
